brief: Rising oil prices, higher yields and geopolitical uncertainty have weighed on high-beta equities for months, pushing the beta factor through one of its most volatile stretches in recent history and driving continued hedging demand as clients positioned for a higher-rate regime. Today's softer payroll print pushed yields lower without being soft enough to spark recession fears, which GS frames as a tailwind for equities given weak market breadth and light net positioning, leaving room for a catch-up rally in laggards. For upside exposure, GS recommends its sector/industry-neutral high-beta basket GSPUBETA. For clients managing beta exposure, which it says sits at the 83rd percentile of its 5-year range in GS's Prime book (a separate chart puts Prime book beta exposure near the 90th percentile), GS recommends hedging with its Beta-ex-AI pair GSPUBETX, which has underperformed the beta basket while keeping high correlation to it. High-beta themes stay linked to the AI complex and high-momentum, and the beta pair's correlation to momentum has stayed strongly positive in recent years.
